meta.note: R1 is a hard blocker: the rail component throws during render, so every downstream behaviour (dot count, click jump, scroll highlight, long-session density, narrow window, dark theme, reload rebuild, 0/1-message boundaries, fast scroll) is measured against a rail that never mounts. Those items are reported as blocked-by-R1 / untested rather than as separate defects, because their own behaviour could not be observed.

checks.title: Right-side dot timeline appears at all
checks.expected: A milestone rail with [data-rail-list] and N [data-rail-dot] renders inside the shell overlay when a conversation with user messages is open
checks.actual: Rail host element exists (8px wide, z-index 11, position absolute at x=276..284) but contains no list and zero dots; a fixed incompatibility notice appears at the bottom-right. The component throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length') at MilestoneRail, which the plugin's own CompatBoundary catches and converts into 'rail disabled'.

reading.notice_text: dsh-milestone 与当前 DSH 版本不兼容，已停用。请升级插件。 Incompatible with this DSH version — please update dsh-milestone.

control_comparison.meaning: the conversation itself renders identically with and without the plugin; the missing dots are the plugin's own failure, not a broken fixture

root_cause.file: src/client/MilestoneRail.tsx line 632 (fixed commit); shipped as lib/client.js
root_cause.why: on DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 the session snapshot exposes `pendingInteraction`; `queue` is gone, so the selector resolves to undefined and `.length` throws
root_cause.evidence: evidence/p07-rootcause-queue.json (bundle snippet, exactly one `.queue)` occurrence, host .d.ts containing only pendingInteraction and no queue field)
root_cause.proposed_fix_not_applied: read pendingInteraction with a null guard, e.g. Boolean(useSession(s => s.pendingInteraction)); source was NOT modified

checks.title: Installation poisons the host's own core packages (environment layer, separate from R1)
checks.expected: Installing the plugin leaves the host's core packages at the host version
checks.actual: `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-milestone` pulls @deepseek-ai/dsh-session@0.1.5-rc.2, dsh-session-projection@0.1.5-rc.2 and dsh-llm@0.1.5-rc.2 into the profile. The loader resolves the same-named bundle rows from the profile directory, so the older copies shadow the host's 0.2.0-rc.2. Result: 2 entries do not activate, the session gateway answers definition-unavailable, and the sidebar shows no sessions at all.

reading.host_stderr_h3: dsh: warning: 2 entries did not activate (typert-loader, image-offload)
reading.side_effect: session/list -> gateway/definition-unavailable; sidebar '暂无会话'; scrollHeight 1000 with 0 rows

checks.mitigation_used: pinned every core package back to 0.2.0-rc.2 via pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides in profile web3; after that the host boots with an empty stderr and the conversation renders normally
checks.caveat: this is an install-time compatibility problem caused by the plugin's dependency ranges, not a defect in its UI code; it is reported separately so it is not confused with R1

checks.title: Dot count corresponds to the number of user messages
checks.actual: Not measurable: zero dots exist. With the fixture that has 3 user messages visible on screen, dot count is 0.

checks.title: Clicking a dot jumps to that message
checks.expected: scrollTop changes and the target user message enters the viewport
checks.actual: Not measurable: there are no dots to click.

checks.title: Current dot highlights while scrolling, keeps up with the wheel
checks.expected: The nearest question in the viewport lights up; the active index stays unique
checks.actual: Not measurable: no dots. Scrolling to 50% of a 4261px-tall conversation changed nothing (0 dots, 0 active).

checks.title: Long session (40+ user messages): density, spacing, no overlap
checks.expected: Dots evenly spaced, clickable, not overlapping
checks.actual: Not measurable: no dots. The 44-turn fixture exists on disk but the sidebar renders session titles as '未命名', so the 44-turn conversation was not opened; the long-session reading is therefore absent for two reasons (no dots, and the specific fixture was not reached).

checks.title: Narrow windows 1000 / 760 / 600 and dark theme visibility, no covering of the text column
checks.expected: Rail stays visible and does not cover the conversation; readable in dark theme
checks.actual: At 1440px the rail host occupies x=276..284 (8px) and overlaps the conversation column by 4px, but it is empty. At 1000 / 760 / 600 the rail host is not even laid out (rail_rect null) while the incompatibility notice still renders. Dark theme at 600px behaves the same (notice present, 0 dots). No dot visibility question can be answered.

checks.title: Rebuild after refresh and after a cold host restart
checks.expected: The rail is rebuilt on reload; preferences survive
checks.actual: Reload ×1 reproduced the same state: 0 dots, list absent, incompatibility notice present. A second reload and a cold restart of the host were not run separately, so the preference-survival half is untested.

checks.title: Boundary cases: 0 and 1 user messages
checks.expected: 0 messages: nothing rendered, no error. 1 message: exactly one dot
checks.actual: Not measurable: the rail throws before it can decide how many dots to draw, so the 0-message and 1-message branches are never reached. Fixtures sess-ms-zero and sess-ms-one exist on disk.

checks.title: Fast scrolling on a very long conversation: no page errors, no freeze, active index unique
checks.expected: No pageerror, no stall, exactly one active dot
checks.actual: Not measurable as designed. One relevant observation: across every run the page reported 0 pageerrors, because the throw happens inside a React error boundary rather than escaping to window.onerror. The absence of pageerrors is therefore NOT evidence that the plugin is healthy.

summary.headline: On DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 the rail never mounts: one unguarded session-snapshot field (`queue`) throws during render and the plugin's own compatibility boundary disables the whole timeline.
not_a_defect: the empty conversation page seen in the earlier partial run was a fixture problem (synthetic events missing turn/end reason), not a plugin problem
the missing sessions in the sidebar after a plain install are the dependency-shadowing problem in R1b, which disappears once core packages are pinned to the host version
